title: Wanted -> A Board Career: The Definitive Playbook for Landing a Board Seat
description: Have you ever thought about serving on a corporate, nonprofit, or advisory board, but didn’t know where to begin? Whether you’re seeking influence, impact, or a second act after an accomplished career, this playbook will show you how to land a board seat that’s right for you. Anyone can join a board if you know how to crack the code. Wanted → A Board Career is not just about gaining a title. It’s about shaping the future of organizations while creating meaning, legacy, and impact in your own life. This step-by-step playbook will help you: Understand the different types of boards and how to target the right ones for you. Translate your career accomplishments into board-ready skills. Build a powerful narrative that attracts attention from nominating committees. Navigate networking and board search consultants (recruiters) with ease. Position yourself as a trusted board member who adds value from day one. This book shows you how to claim your seat in the boardroom. The demand has never been higher. Organizations are transforming at lightning speed and they need your insight, your leadership, and your vision to guide them into the future. What Board Directors are saying about this comprehensive guide: “An easy-to-read ‘how-to’ without ever being pedantic—well written, well organized, and truly comprehensive. I’ve never read a book that starts with ‘why a board’ and ends with ‘onboarding and the work really begins.’ It’s a great playbook, and like all great playbooks, it leaves room for readers to apply their own talent and creativity.” - Stephanie Streeter, Public, private and non-profit board director and former CEO, Libbey Inc. “A must-read roadmap for rising leaders who want a seat at the table.” - Alison Levin, Private board director, nonprofit board chair and President

title: The Board Seat.: A Plain-English Handbook for California HOA Directors: Board Member Dutie
cats: Practical Law Guides for Real Estate
description: A procedural state, and a fee-shifting one. You are implementing an inspection regime whose deadline has already passed, in an insurance market that has broken in parts of the state, funded by money you often have to actually ask the members for. Being a California HOA director is harder now than at any point in the last forty years. This is a working handbook for doing it properly, and for staying out of trouble while you do. Why procedure matters more here In an action to enforce the governing documents, the prevailing party generally recovers attorney fees. That cuts both ways. An assessment that was substantively necessary but procedurally defective is a losing case - and it is the association's members who pay the fees. Most director trouble in California is not about making the wrong decision. It is about making a defensible decision the wrong way. title: THE SERIOUS DIRECTOR: How to Win a Board Seat and Earn It (The Eleventh Seat: Corporate Go
description: If you think a board seat is the natural next step in a distinguished career, this book will save you years of wasted effort — and help you earn a seat worth having. Most accomplished executives approach board search the way they approached every other professional challenge: with hard work, a strong resume, and a broad network. Most are unprepared for what they find. Board search is opaque, relationship-driven, and fiercely competitive in ways that reward precision over pedigree. And once you land a seat, the work itself demands a completely different kind of thinking than anything your executive career prepared you for. The Serious Director is the no-flattery field guide to both challenges — written by two of the most respected names in corporate governance education. Robert G. Eccles (Visiting Professor, Oxford Saïd Business School; former Harvard Business School Professor) and Shiva Rajgopal (Roy Bernard Kester and T. W. Byrnes Professor of Accounting and Auditing, Columbia Business School) have spent decades teaching governance to executives, CFOs, audit committee chairs, and aspiring directors. This book is the distillation of that work — brought together for the reader who cannot be in one of their classrooms. Part One: Getting the Seat The book opens with the unvarnished truth about board search: the identity shift from operator to fiduciary, the ten struggles every candidate encounters (and why most interpret normal friction as personal failure), the difference between an executive résumé and a board CV, and how to read a proxy statement as a targeting tool. title: Earn Your Seat at the Table: A Comprehensive Guide for Executives Preparing for Board Dire
description: In "Earn Your Seat at the Table," Paul Gurrola provides an insightful examination of the true requirements for securing and excelling in a corporate board position. Dispelling common myths about the importance of resumes and titles, Gurrola emphasizes that boards are not in search of the most decorated executives. Instead, they seek strategic thinkers who are capable of anticipating future challenges, question prevailing assumptions, and lead effectively through uncertainty. Drawing from over 20 years of board directorship experience and coaching hundreds of aspiring directors through Corporate Boards USA, Gurrola delivers a practical, no-fluff guide packed with tools, case studies, and insider wisdom. Whether you’re a seasoned executive eyeing your first seat or a current director ready to level up, this book gives you the framework to translate your experience into boardroom impact. You’ll learn how to reframe your story from operator to strategist, avoid toxic board environments, lead with credibility in your first 90 days, navigate power dynamics with quiet influence, and tackle modern issues like cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and crisis oversight. The boardroom is evolving. title: THE BOARD PACKET TEST: How Directors Know Whether Management Is Informing the Board or Man
description: You have been in enough board meetings to know the feeling. The packet arrives. It is polished, thorough, professionally produced. Management presents. The room nods. The vote passes. And somewhere in the drive home, a quiet question surfaces: did that packet inform me, or manage me? Most directors have felt that doubt and had no way to act on it. The Board Packet Test gives you one. This is not another book about what good governance looks like in theory. It is a working diagnostic — built from more than fifty governance seminars and years of direct work with corporate boards — that tells you, packet by packet, meeting by meeting, whether the materials in front of you are built to inform your judgment or quietly replace it. Inside, you will learn to spot the specific, repeatable patterns that separate an honest packet from a captured one: — The anchoring effect of an executive summary, and how it can shape a room's conclusion before a single question is asked. — The missing page: the rejected alternative, the softened risk, the metric that quietly stopped appearing between quarters and how to find it before the meeting, not after the restatement. — Information drift: how disclosure erodes into reassurance over successive quarters without anyone ever telling an outright lie. — Why board portals are never neutral filing systems, and how their design can bury exactly what a director most needs to find. — How to use AI as an examiner, not a summarizer — the single most consequential distinction in how artificial intelligence should and shouldn't be used in the boardroom, including a ready-to-use governance prompt built specifically for pre-meeting preparation. title: YOUR FIRST BOARD SEAT: The Executive Pl aybook for Private & Public Company Directors
description: Your First Board Seat is the practical guide every executive needs before stepping into the boardroom. Moving from executive to board director requires more than experience—it demands a new mindset, a strong understanding of governance, and the ability to lead through influence rather than authority. Drawing on over twenty-five years of boardroom and executive leadership experience, David Catzel provides a practical roadmap to help first-time directors succeed with confidence. Inside, you'll learn how to: Transition from operator to director. Understand your legal and fiduciary responsibilities. Evaluate board opportunities before accepting them. Work effectively with CEOs and fellow directors. Ask better questions and make stronger decisions. Manage risk and protect yourself as a director.
